utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Call the case, please, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is case number IT-98-34-T, the Prosecutor versus Naletilic and Martinovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Could we have the witness, please. Before the witness comes, I must say that this week we have five witnesses, and the recess is coming. So whenever we finish those five witnesses, we'll break. Tomorrow morning, we'll be in Courtroom III, 2.15 in the afternoon. On Wednesday, we'll come back to Courtroom I at 12.00 sharp. We will finish earlier, at 4.45.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Witness. Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon. Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Would you please make the solemn declaration in accordance with the paper the usher is showing you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You may sit down, please. Yes, Mr. Seric.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. Good afternoon, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, you will now be shown a piece of paper with your name on it. Look at it. Don't read it aloud. Just tell us if that is indeed your name on it and just say, "Yes."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MJ
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: I will ask you some questions, and we must go slow but not too slow, enough, however, to enable the interpreters to keep up with both you and me. We have to mind that there is a break between your -- my question and your answer, and the best way to go about it will be if you follow this red light on my microphone. When I switch it off, it will mean that I have finished my question and then you can begin answering. That is also important for your protection, because the Chamber has granted you the protective measures that you asked for.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I'd like now to go into some particulars. Could we go into private session, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. We will go to the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Witness, will you please wait for me to finish my question. Relax. Take it easy. There is no need for any rush. During the attack of the aggressor of the Serbian and the Yugoslav People's Army on Mostar, where were you and what was happening to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MJ
utterances.text: During the attack of the Serb aggressor I joined the 2nd Battalion of the HVO.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Were you called up or did you volunteer?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MJ
utterances.text: I volunteered.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Did you hold any duty, any rank?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MJ
utterances.text: Just a foot soldier.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Wait a little, please. And until when did you stay with the HVO?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MJ
utterances.text: With the HVO, I was until mid-June, because I had some trouble with my back.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: What year was it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MJ
utterances.text: 1993. Or 1992. I don't know. I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Does the date of the 9th of May, 1993 ring any bell? What do you know about that date? What happened that day? That is, what did you see with your own eyes and hear with your own ears?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MJ
utterances.text: That day I heard gunfire. Some troops had entered the building but I didn't know any one of them. And they asked for my identity card. They saw my identity card. They realised I was with the HVO. They did nothing, but they searched the whole building. They went to all the flats but they take anybody. They just looked around. That was what happened that day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We have a problem with the channels. It seems to me the sound of the witness is louder than the translators. So the two voices mingle together. We could not hear clearly. Yes. You may try it again.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: So you described to us what you personally saw and hear happened on the 9th of May, 1993. Can you repeat it for the Chamber?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MJ
utterances.text: That day, I heard gunfire, and after awhile some troops came into the building, four or five of them. And since I lived on the ground floor, they came to my door first. They asked to see my identity papers. They saw my HVO card. They did nothing. And then they did a round of all the apartments. They were there two or three minutes, perhaps five. They said nothing and nothing.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: I am now asking. You said that you couldn't remember which mid-June did you stay with the HVO? So in this May 1993, what did you do?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MJ
utterances.text: In May. I was in the HVO.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Did you work as a driver at the time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MJ
utterances.text: Yes. The ambulance driver. No. No. No, no. No. I began to drive the ambulance car in June.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Which year?

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: And what happened to you during that period of time until July?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MJ
utterances.text: Until July, well, I had this problem with my back so that I wasn't in the HVO. I was on a sick leave. And after ten days or 15, I was taken up to drive the ambulance car for the war hospital of the HVO in Mostar.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: And you did that until when?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MJ
utterances.text: Until the 1st of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: And what happened that 1st of July, 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MJ
utterances.text: I was duty driver at the surgery in Mostar, and they called and asked me to come to Bijeli Brijeg to get the instruments because that nurse had that bag. And when we got there to Partizansko, that's where the monument was. There was a checkpoint. And they asked for my papers. They asked what my ethnicity was. I gave them my driving licence. They got me out of the ambulance car and put me onto a bus.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: And do you know who those soldiers were?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MJ
utterances.text: I'm 99 per cent sure they all came from Livno.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: And after that, what happened to you? What did they do to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MJ
utterances.text: They put me in the ambulance car, and one of those soldiers took away the ambulance car and the nurse to Bijeli Brijeg. And when my boss heard that I'd been captured, he got some men from up there to set me free. And this soldier said that my bus had left, and I dared not call out.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: It is not quite clear where you were and what are you talking about. What do you mean your bus left?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MJ
utterances.text: Well, that bus that I boarded when, my bus came from Bijeli Brijeg to ask where I was, he said that bus had left, allegedly, that I was in, that that bus had left, that it wasn't there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: And where were you taken in that bus?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MJ
utterances.text: I was taken towards Rondo where he stopped. And those soldiers were going into buildings and bringing Muslims out.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Was the bus full?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MJ
utterances.text: They took me off the ambulance car around 10.00, and that bus was full around 6.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: And after that what happened to you and those other people in the bus?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MJ
utterances.text: We were all taken to the camp at Dretelj.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: And where were you put in Dretelj?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MJ
utterances.text: I was put in, vacated in empty hangars.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: What were the conditions there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MJ
utterances.text: They were bad.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us what was bad? What was it that was bad there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MJ
utterances.text: Food, water, drink, communication. You had no communication, the door closed. Four or 500 of us inside and it was hot.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: And what kind of hangars were those?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MJ
utterances.text: Well, I suppose of the former army. Oils. One could see it was greasy so it must have been for oils, for vehicles.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Did anyone mistreat you, beat you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MJ
utterances.text: No. No. Personally, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: And how long did you stay in Dretelj?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MJ
utterances.text: I stayed 19 days in Dretelj.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: And then what happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MJ
utterances.text: Then the order came that all the prisoners from the municipality of Mostar should be transferred to the Heliodrom.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: And where were you put up in the Heliodrom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MJ
utterances.text: We were put in the gym at the Heliodrom.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: And what were the conditions there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MJ
utterances.text: Excellent compared with Dretelj.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: And what was food like? Could you have any visits? Could you receive any parcels?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MJ
utterances.text: I received parcels every day.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Were you taken to work, to some unit, from the Heliodrom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MJ
utterances.text: When I arrived from Dretelj, I spent there three or four days and we couldn't go out anywhere. They wouldn't let us go work anywhere until Vinko Martinovic heard that I was there. And in about four days' time or thereabouts, he got and sent a driver to bring me to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Can you explain what you mean sent a driver to fetch you? What happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MJ
utterances.text: Well, I guess he heard that I was down there, so he sent a man to bring me. And the man came in a car, showed his card that he would take me there and bring me back, and we went.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Did you used to know Vinko Martinovic before?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MJ
utterances.text: Well, we weren't all that great friends, but we knew each other well.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: And when you were brought to the unit, the first time, what happened? Describe the first day to us?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MJ
utterances.text: The first day we arrived there we settled, drank coffee and then he said, "Well, you've got any of your pals there and they're loyal to you, bring them over there because they'll be safer here than if they go somewhere, God knows where."

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Mind that you do not say your name. And did you go there again?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MJ
utterances.text: The next day I got together some 15, 16 people who -- that I was sure that who -- that would work, that they would not be into any Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French English transcripts mischief. Then Vinko, Stela's driver came and took us to his base.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Do you remember the driver?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MJ
utterances.text: Well, I can't really. I guess I'd recognise him, but --

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: You don't know his first name, his last name, his nickname?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MJ
utterances.text: I don't, by Joe I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: How was it possible that after the first day you came again and then again? How is it possible? Did you report again what happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MJ
utterances.text: This whole team which volunteered, they went there all the time. They all volunteered, and they went regularly there, as long as I was at the Heliodrom, for a whole month.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Did you know and any of those other prisoners, did you -- would you ever spend the night there during that time, you or one of those prisoners?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MJ
utterances.text: No. While I was there, nobody stayed overnight there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: How long did you -- for how long a period of time did you go to Vinko Martinovic's base?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MJ
utterances.text: I went there until the end, that is, on the 19th of July, I was moved from Dretelj to Heliodrom. And on the 23rd or 24th of July until the end of August, I was at Vinko Martinovic, Stela's.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Did you go there every day, I mean every single day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MJ
utterances.text: Every day except for weekends.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Will you describe so that everybody in the courtroom can hear, and especially the Chamber, an average day did you spend at Vinko Martinovic's unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MJ
utterances.text: Well, we -- we worked there. We maintained vehicles. If you needed to do something about the car, some small repair to be tempered with those cars, we did something. We did all sorts of odd jobs.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Were you paid in any way? Did you get any kind of remuneration?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MJ
utterances.text: Every day I'd get cigarettes and food. And moreover, my wife came with children, and she took home bagfuls of food when there was nothing to be found in town.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Were you taken across the Bulevar to the front line?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MJ
utterances.text: I drove a car, but I never got near the front line.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: And during that period of time during which you went to the unit, do you know if any other prisoners were taken to the Bulevar next to the health centre?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MJ
utterances.text: While I was there, I can guarantee that nobody was taken there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Did you personally see or hear, whilst you went to that unit and to the base of that unit, that -- any prisoner being wounded or killed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MJ
utterances.text: Nobody was either wounded or killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Did you ever see anyone mistreat the prisoners?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MJ
utterances.text: Once we were sitting on the wall next to Stela's base, and the military police came up, and the guy, I don't remember him but I think he came from Stolac, the military police mistreated him and abused him verbally, "Balija" this, "Balija" that. And they left. And after 20 minutes Stela came and we talked about that, and he immediately switched on his car and went after him round the town for two or three hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: And what happened? Did he find him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MJ
utterances.text: No, he didn't. He didn't. But he looked for them.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: And why? Why did he look for them? What did he want?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MJ
utterances.text: Well, he didn't want -- he didn't want anyone in that group to be abused or teased or anything. You get it? We were totally protected.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Could you describe the conditions in the course of the day while you were in the unit at Vinko Martinovic's? Could you tell us what the food was like?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MJ
utterances.text: We ate the same food that the soldiers did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Where did you spend the day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MJ
utterances.text: We were all on the grounds, about 20 or 30 metres away. That's where everything took place.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Were you under guard? Were there any armed guards? Were the guards who were watching over you and would point their weapons at you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MJ
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: You mentioned your wife and your children. What did this involve? Did they go to visit you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MJ
utterances.text: Every day. My wife and children visited me every day. I would go home, because that was my work. You would sort of maintain a car. And I would go home twice a week to have a bath. But a driver drove me there since it wasn't safe for me to go there on foot. Vinko never allowed me to go on foot because somebody could have killed me. Somebody could have inflicted harm on me.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: You didn't say how someone could have selected you, picked you up.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MJ
utterances.text: Well, there were soldiers there. Who knows where they were from? They all ended up in Mostar. The Muslims and Croats, they all ended up in Mostar. From Duvno, from Livno, they all went there. Who knows what the army was there. It was easy for me.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: So it means that you weren't safe if you were not escorted. Your papers could have been checked.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MJ
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Why did you have to go and have a bath at home? Couldn't you have done that at the base?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MJ
utterances.text: Well, as I could go home, it was ten, 15 minutes away, my house wasn't far away, I would go home. Then a driver would wait for me. I'd have a shower and then I'd return. My wife came to visit me every day.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Did you personally feel safe in the base?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MJ
utterances.text: Yes, I was a hundred per cent safe.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: A minute ago, my colleague said -- it hasn't entered the transcript -- but a minute ago you mentioned the fact that you were afraid of someone meeting you and check your papers in the street and capturing you, and also that Muslims were being prosecuted by some people from Bosnia. You mentioned some people from Bosnia. Could you say what you meant when you said that someone was prosecuting someone, that someone was -- you mentioned someone from Bosnia. That someone --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MJ
utterances.text: Well, these Croats who had been expelled from Bosnia, it was difficult to walk around at the time, you know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. What was Vinko Martinovic's relationship towards you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MJ
utterances.text: It was excellent, excellent. Maybe it diverged from the other people who were there, but it was all within certain limits.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: What was the position of the other detainees? How did Vinko Martinovic treat them and how did other soldiers treat them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MJ
utterances.text: The same way as they treated me, because these people went with me, and they were guaranteed that everything would be fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: How is it that you were released from there, from the Heliodrom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MJ
utterances.text: That day a jeep turned up. There was some party, an MDS. Paraga, I don't know who led them. It wasn't Paraga, I can't remember the name. He said nothing will be done to him. He will be protected. And so I signed a paper on that day and I left.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: What happened after? What happened to you after that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MJ
utterances.text: I was at home for a few days. Then I had to go work in the garage, take out motors, wash cars. I had to live from something, so I had to work.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: After that did you have any problems, problems of any kind?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MJ
utterances.text: Two or three times the troops came to my door. I said, "I'm with Stela." They returned.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: While you were in the unit, or later on when you were released from the Heliodrom, did you personally see or hear Vinko Martinovic or his soldiers expelling, driving Muslims out of their flats?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MJ
utterances.text: As I personally knew Vinko, and I know his entire team, 90 per cent of them, I never saw them in flats. I never saw them driving anyone out.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Did you personally see Vinko Martinovic assist Muslims? Did they turn to him for help?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MJ
utterances.text: While I was on the base, five to ten, or sometimes 20 men would come and they had contact with him. But I wasn't present. I saw that they were there and they were asking him for something.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. This concludes my examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Cross-examination. Mr. Bos.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I'll be using one exhibit for this cross-examination, which is Exhibit P567.1, and I think the Defence was informed about this, and I hope that the Judges will have -- this is the Heliodrom lock-up, so I hope that the Judges will have it in front of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Witness.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MJ
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Witness, my name is Roeland Bos, from the Office of the Prosecution, and I will ask you some questions in cross-examination. To start off with, you said that your relationship with Mr. Vinko Martinovic was excellent. Could you tell the Court: Did you have any personal relationship with Mr. Vinko Martinovic before the war started?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MJ
utterances.text: No kind of relationship before the war. When we met, we would greet each other and that's all.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: When you say you would greet each other, is that because you knew each other or you knew -- your families were acquainted or was it just that you knew each other by face?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MJ
utterances.text: Our families didn't know each other, but I personally did know Stela.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: And how did you know him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MJ
utterances.text: Well, Mostar isn't a big city. Everyone knew everyone else in the town.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Well, let me then ask you: When was the first time that you met Mr. Vinko Martinovic? What was the occasion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MJ
utterances.text: I don't know what you mean "The first time." During the war you mean or --

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: No, the very first time you met Mr. Vinko Martinovic.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MJ
utterances.text: That was a long time ago. I can't remember that. It's impossible to remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Well, were you friends in school or did you -- are we talking about the age that you were 15 or 25? Could you give us a bit more information on that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MJ
utterances.text: Well, when we were young men.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Did you both attend the same school?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MJ
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Would you see each other very often in the neighbourhood?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MJ
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Witness, why do you think that Mr. Vinko Martinovic, when you were at the Heliodrom, asked specifically for you? Could you -- you think there is any reason for that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MJ
utterances.text: There's no reason, that's for sure. Quite simply we were -- we were friends and that's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Now, Witness, is it correct that you were -- is it correct you were taken to the Heliodrom around the 20th of July? Correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MJ
utterances.text: On the 19th of July, we were transferred from Dretelj to the Heliodrom.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Now, you testified when you arrived at the Heliodrom the witness were much better, and then you said that you received parcels every day. What did you mean by that? What did you receive and from whom did you receive it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MJ
utterances.text: Well, the people who had been trained in the HVO, when they heard that I was there, they brought cigarettes. They'd bring clothes, food. That's what I was referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: So you received these cigarettes and food from HVO soldiers; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MJ
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: And were these HVO soldiers guarding the Heliodrom camp or were these soldiers coming from outside to enter the Heliodrom camp and then talk to prisoners?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MJ
utterances.text: They were soldiers from outside, and they came when they heard that we were there, and they spoke to us and asked us what they need -- what we needed and said that they would bring us provisions.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Did these HVO soldiers simply enter the camp out any difficulties?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MJ
utterances.text: No one could enter without an identity card. I wasn't at the gate. What do I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Now, Witness, you've testified that around the 24th or the 25th of July was the first time that you actually were taken to the headquarters of Mr. Vinko Martinovic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MJ
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: And from that moment on, all the way up until the end of August, you worked. Every day you worked for Stela's unit, except for the Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French English transcripts weekends; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MJ
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Now, what happened in the weekends? Is it your testimony that during the weekends no prisoners were taken out of the Heliodrom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MJ
utterances.text: Not this group of ours. I don't know about the others.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Let me ask it this way: While you were at the Heliodrom on the weekends, did you ever see other detainees being taken, being taken out for labour?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MJ
utterances.text: I didn't see them at the gate exactly, so I couldn't see whether they were taking them anywhere. There were people walking around on the grounds, but how am I to know where somebody was taking somebody? But usually on the weekends no one was taken anywhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Witness, while you were at the Heliodrom, did you ever hear of a group of prisoners from the Stolac area which were wearing blue pilot uniforms and were referred to as the Blue Orchestra?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MJ
utterances.text: I can't remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Witness, you didn't say you could remember the name of the driver who took you to Stela's headquarters. Does the name Dinko Knezevic, does that recall anything?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MJ
utterances.text: The name is familiar to me, but I'm not certain.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Could the witness be shown Exhibit P567.1.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Witness, yes, there is an exhibit I'm going to refer to which is right in front of you there, and let me first ask you a question before we open the document. Is it correct that the group of prisoners that were taken to Stela's headquarters in this period that you were also taken there would vary between 15 and 25 prisoners per day, the number of detainees that were taken to --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MJ
utterances.text: Yes, something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Very well. Now, if you could look at this Exhibit P567.1, and in particular I'd like you to look at the page of which the last digits are -- let me just have a look -- 5055. Witness, this logbook is a logbook which was kept at the Heliodrom where the names of the prisoners were written down, the names of the prisoners that were taken out for labour were written down. And we're in open session, so I don't want you to refer to your name, but if you could look at this page ending with 5055. Is it correct that in the right-hand column your name appeared under number 1?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: You've testified that -- that all the prisoners who were taken to Mr. Martinovic's base volunteered. Is it your testimony that these 21 prisoners all volunteered?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Now, if you've been there for more than a month, working every day during the week, I presume you got acquainted with several other prisoners who were working there. Could you please go through this list and see how many detainees you recognise the name of? And maybe just mention the number if you recognise the person. Sir, just to be sure, I only want you -- please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MJ
utterances.text: Yes. Well, these names here don't mean anything to me. I can't remember. These names mean nothing to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Well, Witness, just to be sure that you've been looking at the right -- at the right column, what I actually asked you to do, and maybe I should have been a bit more clear, is to look only at the 21 names which are written under the ATG Vinko Skrobo where you appear as number 1. That particular list of names, would you look at those names and see if you recognise any of those names?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MJ
utterances.text: I can't remember a single name. This is all -- they all went. They all left.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Well, Witness, if you don't seem to recall any of the names on this list, could you then tell us which names you do recall of prisoners who were also taken to Stela's headquarters in that period that you were taken there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MJ
utterances.text: I've got four sons at home, and they need jobs, but this took place ten years ago, and I can't remember it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: My apologies, but I didn't really understand your answer. You said you've got four sons. Are you afraid to mention names? Because we can go into private session if that's the case.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MJ
utterances.text: No. I said I had a house and four sons. And on the same day, I forget how to call one of my sons, let alone if we mention some of these people. How am supposed to remember the name. That's what I wanted to say.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Very well. Now, you've testified that during that period that you were there you worked in the garage. Where was this garage located in relation to the headquarters of Mr. Vinko Martinovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MJ
utterances.text: Well, right next to the base. It wasn't a big workshop. It was a temporary installation. There was a cover for the rain. It wasn't a big place. It was possible to work there and that's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: And with how many persons at the same time would you work in this garage?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MJ
utterances.text: I worked on my own. I'd repair the cars. Others would get the body work prepared. Others would deal with the colour. And I would polish the cars myself, on my own.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Were you good at what you were doing, when you said you repaired the cars, you polished the cars? Were you considered an expert?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MJ
utterances.text: Well, in wartime conditions, yes. I was a good worker.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Now, Witness, if you say that you -- that you would basically do the work alone, I would wonder if we just saw a list of 20 names and you agreed that the number would vary between the 15 and the 25 detainees that would be taken to Stela's headquarters, what were all these other people doing that were taken to Mr. Vinko Martinovic's headquarters?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MJ
utterances.text: Well, everyone had something to do. Some people would sit down and have coffee. Another person would wash a cash. Another person would sweep the yard. Everyone had something to do.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Would prisoners sometimes also be taken out on assignment with people from the Vinko Skrobo units? Somewhere outside of where the headquarters was.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MJ
utterances.text: I don't personally remember that taking place.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Did you ever talk with the prisoners at the end of the day when you went back to the Heliodrom about the work you'd done that day, what you had experienced that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MJ
utterances.text: I never spoke about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Witness, if -- while you were working at -- on what kind of cars or vehicles did you work in the garage? Was this military vehicles or private vehicles?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MJ
utterances.text: They were soldiers' vehicles. If it had been damaged, then it would be necessary to repair something. But usually these were all private vehicles.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: If they were private vehicles, did these vehicles belong to the soldiers who were in the unit of Vinko Martinovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Did Mr. Vinko Martinovic have a car as well?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: How many cars did he have?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MJ
utterances.text: Drove one.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Sorry. I --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MJ
utterances.text: He drove one. You can't drive five cars. He drove one. I saw him driving one car. I saw him in one car.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: So -- but you don't know whether he owned more than one car?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MJ
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: You've testified that your wife would come and visit you every day whilst you were working at the headquarters of Vinko Skrobo. I think you've also said that she was given food every day. Where was this -- all this food coming from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MJ
utterances.text: Well, Stela, in the headquarters, had something from humanitarian aid, I think. But there were tins. There was sweet stuff. There was cigarettes. There was all sorts of things.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: I think you said that he had food from the humanitarian aid. Would that mean that every day or every week boxes of food would arrive at the headquarters coming from an humanitarian aid organisation? Is that how I understand it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MJ
utterances.text: That's what I assume. I'm not claiming that that's right, but there was food there. How do I know? But there was food.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Witness, you said that you served for the Vinko Skrobo until the end of August. What happened after that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MJ
utterances.text: I said a party turned up. MDS, that was its name. And it said, "Whoever wants to join this party, the Muslims will be protected." I registered, and that was it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Where did these representatives of the MDS show up, at the Heliodrom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MJ
utterances.text: At the Heliodrom.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Do you recall the name of this person or were there more persons than just one?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MJ
utterances.text: There were a number of them, two or three, but I can't remember the names. I don't know what they were called. Well, now if I saw them, now I'd recognise them.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: But it is your testimony that this was the end of September or early October that these people from the MDS showed up?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MJ
utterances.text: That's how I went. I don't know when exactly they turned up, but they turned up at the Heliodrom sometime late August or --

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Besides you, other prisoners also joined this MDS?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MJ
utterances.text: Well, that day, about seven or eight of us, I think, signed up.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Do you recall any prisoners who refused to sign up for this Muslim democratic party?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MJ
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Witness, did you ever work for any other unit except for the Vinko Skrobo unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MJ
utterances.text: I worked up there in a garage, but it was nobody's unit. In a garage, later on. I went from the Heliodrom. I joined that garage, but I don't think it was anybody's unit. We worked there earning some money.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Was this while you were still detained at the Heliodrom or was this after you were released from the Heliodrom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MJ
utterances.text: After I came out.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: And when was the date that you actually were released from the Heliodrom? Do you recall that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MJ
utterances.text: No, not exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Do you recall approximately how many days it was after the last time you served for the Vinko Skrobo unit? Are we talking about several months or a few weeks or a few days?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MJ
utterances.text: A few days. And as soon as I left, I started looking for a job.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Witness, I'd like to you look again at this logbook.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Maybe the usher can assist.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: I'd ask you to look at page 01535122. First let's look at 5117. Witness, looking at page 5117 of Exhibit 567.1, is it correct that there is the name ATG Vinko Skrobo and your name here is listed as number 2?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Now, this is the be try of 30 August, 1993. Now, Witness, under number 1 it says the name "Vlado Fink." Do you recall that name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MJ
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Was he one of the detainees who, just like you, would be taken to -- who volunteered to work for Vinko Skrobo and would be taken to that unit every day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MJ
utterances.text: I can't remember exactly. Perhaps once.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: What do you mean by saying "perhaps once"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MJ
utterances.text: I think that he was taken once. I can't remember. It was ten years ago. Who can remember?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Did you know him from working in the garage?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MJ
utterances.text: I knew Vlado from before.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Witness, looking at that same list, could you look at the person under number 4. His name is Zlatko Cerkic. Do you recall that name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MJ
utterances.text: It rings a bell, but I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Witness, I'd like you to turn a few pages now and move -- perhaps the usher can assist you again, and move to the page ending with 5122. And I'd like you to look in the right-hand corner of that page where it says "ATG Benko Penavic."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MJ
utterances.text: What right-hand corner?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MJ
utterances.text: Right-hand corner it says at one point "ATG Benko Penavic," and again there's a list of names. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MJ
utterances.text: I do, I do, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Is it correct that your name is under 5? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French English transcripts

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: And is it also correct that the two other names which I just mentioned to you are listed under number 1 and number 4?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Now, Witness, and we wouldn't go through it, but on this day, you were listed as working for the ATG Benko Penavic. Does that name mean anything to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MJ
utterances.text: Well, I know the unit. Later on I worked, but I didn't know it was called that. I didn't know it was called that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: And is it correct that you -- that you worked for several days for this unit, as of the 31st of August?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MJ
utterances.text: Well, when I went, I did work. I had to work. I had to earn my living, and they paid us there.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Witness, do you know the reason why you were moving from the ATG -- working for the ATG Vinko Skrobo on the 3rd of August and for the ATG Benko Penavic on the 31st of August and also with you Mr. Cerkic and Mr. Vlado Fink? Why did the three of you move from Vinko Skrobo to the ATG Benko Penavic? Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MJ
utterances.text: I wasn't transferred. I was released from Vinko Skrobo. And later, I had to work in order to make some money, and I moved to that unit. But I wasn't transferred.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Witness, just before you testified that you were making money after you were released from the Heliodrom, but this is a logbook taking out prisoners from the Heliodrom. So in this period, the beginning of September you were still a prisoner at the Heliodrom; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MJ
utterances.text: I remember that in late August I was released to go home. What day it was, who can remember? It was ten years ago. I can't remember what I had for lunch yesterday, let alone.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Witness, do you recall what kind of work you would do for this Benko Penavic unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MJ
utterances.text: Well, again mechanic things with this, something. Taking out engines. Whatever broke down, we tried to fix it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Where was this garage located of the Benko Penavic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MJ
utterances.text: The place is called Balinovac, towards Siroki, up there as you come out of Mostar.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I've let these questions to be asked about a completely different unit, which have nothing to do with my client, that unit, and I see -- I done see what direction the counsel is leading to. What does that have to do with my direct examination and challenging the credibility of this witness? So my objection is, why ask questions of the Benko Penavic unit?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Bos, perhaps you could shed some light on this issue for us.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, it wasn't clear from his testimony whether he worked for another unit, and that's what I wanted to clarify and for the second thing, I think it is important for the Prosecution. The Benko Penavic unit is an important unit. And that's why I asked some questions about it. I have some more questions. Not too many, but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. You may some a few more questions but we are approaching the time for the break. Would you prefer to ask your questions or until you finish your cross-examination we can break.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: I think if I can finish this cross-examination. It wasn't take too much longer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, you can proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Witness, do you know who the head of this Benko Penavic unit was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MJ
utterances.text: They called him "Baja."

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Did you ever meet this man named Baja?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MJ
utterances.text: No, not personally, by saw him two or three times.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Did you see this Baja very often with Mr. Vinko Martinovic or did you ever see him with Mr. Vinko Martinovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MJ
utterances.text: No, never saw him with Vinko Martinovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Does the name Convicts Battalion say anything to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MJ
utterances.text: I didn't even know it was called that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: No. I'm just asking. Does the name Convicts Battalion mean anything to you? Did you ever hear that name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MJ
utterances.text: I heard it later when I came out, from Vinko Martinovic, and later on. Some said ATG, some said Convicts. I didn't know who it belonged to nor how was it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: So it's your testimony that up heard from others that the ATGs had something to do with the Convicts Battalion? Is that your testimony?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: I object to the form of the question, Your Honour. That's not what the witness testified. I object to the form of the question and assumes facts not in evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I'm just trying to simply clarify what his answer was because his answer wasn't very clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: The witness said that he did not know the Convicts Battalion at all, the ATG.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Then he continues to say, "I heard it later when I came out, from Vinko Martinovic. Some said ATG, some said Convicts," and I'm just trying to clarify what he meant by that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, you may pursue it along this.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Witness, again my question. Did you hear from others that there was some association between the ATGs and the Convicts Battalion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MJ
utterances.text: I really don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Witness, did you know any of the members of the Vinko Skrobo unit while you were working -- while you were working there? Did you get to know some of these people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MJ
utterances.text: No, I didn't really meet anyone, but I knew everyone like that. I didn't really socialise among them. I had no time to talk. I was doing my job and they was on the front lines and I was here in the compound. So I didn't, ever.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Did you ever hear of the name of a man named Ernest Takac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MJ
utterances.text: Yes. I heard it. I saw him. He was in the unit too.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Do you know whether Mr. Takac had some sort of command position within the unit? Was he a group leader or something or was he just a soldier of that unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MJ
utterances.text: I haven't the foggiest, really. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: One moment, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We will break now, and we will resume at 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Any re-examination, Mr. Seric?

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Witness, thank you very much for coming to The Hague to give your evidence. When the usher pulls down the blinds, he will show you out of the courtroom. We all wish you a pleasant journey back home.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Any documents to tender, Mr. Seric?

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. Only the plan of the town. It is D2/34.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Any objections Mr. Bos?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. And the exhibit I used was already admitted, so we don't have anything to tender.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. So D2/34 is admitted into evidence under seal. Yes, Mr. Par. Are you ready for your next witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President, I am.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. We will have the next witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Would you please make the solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You may sit down, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Par. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Mr. President. Could we have the ELMO down, please, so that I can see the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MK
utterances.text: Good afternoon to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Before we proceed to work, I wish to inform you that the Chamber has granted you protective measures. In other words, nobody will know your name, your face will not appear in public, and your voice will -- nobody will recognise your voice. Before I start with my questions, you will be shown a paper with your name on it. If it is your name, then just confirm it without saying your name aloud.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MK
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Thank you. And one warning. For the interpreters' sake, we need to speak slowly. We need to make breaks between question and answer, and the best way to do it will be if you look at this red light. When it is off, then you can start answering. I will switch it on and off, and I will give you a sign if you need to slow down.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, could we now go into private session for a moment?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. We will go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
